You are reviewing the VISUAL DESIGN and UX of a desktop backgammon game called nard, before
its first release. I want your opinion, not code. Do not modify any file in this repository.

WHAT IT IS
A backgammon game built as a gift for one specific person: a genuinely strong, lifelong
Iranian backgammon player in his sixties. He agreed to play it on the condition that it
looks good. Visual quality is a functional requirement here, not decoration. He is not a
beginner — no tutorials, no hand-holding, no confetti, no congratulation.

The owner's verdict on the current state, verbatim: "The game looks a lot better than before
but the board still feels a bit cheap." Earlier rounds already fixed: flat procedural
materials (everything is now a real generated texture — walnut, rosewood, khatam marquetry,
camel bone, ebony), missing drag-and-drop, an empty interface, and type that was too small.
So the obvious wins are taken. I need the next layer.

HOW TO LOOK AT IT
1. Screenshots of every screen, current as of now, are in `.shots/review/`. Read
   `.shots/review/index.txt` first — it says what each image is. LOOK AT THE IMAGES; they
   are PNGs and you can open them.
2. A dev server is already running at http://localhost:5173 . You may drive it yourself:
     pnpm shots        # board fixtures -> .shots/
     pnpm live         # the play view, mid-match; --w= --h= --lang=fa --theme= --pick
     pnpm screens      # ladder, end-of-game, review
     pnpm reviewpack   # everything above, into .shots/review/
   Any board state is addressable: http://localhost:5173/?scene=opening (scenes are listed
   in apps/ui/src/dev/scenes.ts), and /gallery shows them all at once.
3. The binding design document is `docs/design-language.md`. Read it. It states the light
   model, the material rules, the geometry and the motion spec. If you think something in it
   is WRONG, say so — it is not sacred, but disagreeing with it should be deliberate.
4. The board is drawn in SVG under `apps/ui/src/board/`. The interface chrome is
   `apps/ui/src/game/Rail.tsx`, `ladder/Ladder.tsx`, `review/Review.tsx`.

You are free to search the web — look at how Backgammon Galaxy, eXtreme Gammon, Apple
Arcade's Backgammon+, chess.com and lichess actually present a board, and at real
photographs of Persian khatam takhteh nard boards. Compare what you see there against what
you see here.

WHAT I WANT BACK
A prioritised critique. For each point:
  - what specifically is wrong or weak, naming the screen and the element;
  - why it reads as cheap / unfinished / amateur, in visual terms (value, contrast,
    spacing, alignment, proportion, edge quality, consistency of light);
  - what to do instead, concretely enough to act on.

Order it by how much it would change a first impression. Be blunt. If something already
works, say so briefly and move on — I do not need reassurance, I need the list of things
that are still wrong.

Two specific things the owner has already flagged, so check them first and tell me if you
see more of the same kind:
  A. The bar — the raised spine down the middle of the board — looks off-centre, and the
     left and right halves appear to "seep into" it. Measure it if you can rather than
     eyeballing: the geometry is in apps/ui/src/board/geometry.ts.
  B. The board overall still reads as slightly cheap despite the real materials.

Finish with the single change you would make first if you could only make one.
